topic: Post-self-apply re-review of §1.5 EXP-623 'published density' subsection — 4 holes self-applied from c1, verify they closed cleanly
our_argument_summary: The §1.5 subsection 'The published density: neutron-star material as walking medium' attacks the dome's published rho_A = 3.4e17 kg/m^3 — neutron-star-density material asserted to function as a medium humans walk through, push aircraft as a slipstream (Job 2), and metric-warp ground distance (Job 3). After the c1 review, decider self-applied 4 holes: H0 (kernel-of-truth tightened from 'kind of move a working theorist would make' to a dimensional-consistency claim), H1 (nuclear saturation density 1.5x/2.3e17 -> 1.3x/2.7e17), H2 ('within a factor of unity' -> 'at the low end of the neutron-star core density band'), H3 ('same gap' -> 'same shape of gap'). H4 (rhetorical sharpening on 'vaporizes') was wontfix per ISS-2758. Re-review confirms H1, H2, H3 landed cleanly; H0 patch introduced a new precision issue ('with c' substitution) flagged below.

dome_code_analysis.calculation_pipeline: Dome publishes rho_A = 3.4e17 kg/m^3 in Core parameters block (model.html ~line 638) as 'aetheric medium density (from RAR constraint g†)'. Tesla principle 3 row at ~line 629 lists the formula rho_A = g0 × rho_bar / g†. rho_bar is undefined on the model page; back-solving for rho_bar yields ~4.16e6 kg/m^3 (denser than Earth's core, thinner than white-dwarf interior, matching no standard physics density). Per c1: this is unauditable from the dome source.
dome_code_analysis.hardcoded_vs_computed: Published value 3.4e17 kg/m^3 is presented as derived from g0 × rho_bar / g† but with an undefined rho_bar. Per c1: the dome carries a CONSISTENT badge (not CONFIRMED) on Tesla principle row 3, the only row containing this derivation — the dome's own labelling pre-flags it as weakest.
dome_code_analysis.escape_clauses: Dome's own CONSISTENT badge on Tesla principle 3 (vs CONFIRMED on rows 1, 2, 4, 5) is the dome's only published acknowledgement that this row is weaker. Per c1.
dome_code_analysis.code_discrepancies: Per c1: none in the EXP-623 quotation of model.html. Current finding (this c2): the patched kernel-of-truth misrepresents the dome's actual derivation pathway (see holes_found H0c2).

holes_found.description: H0 PATCH MISTRANSCRIBES THE DOME'S DERIVATION. The c1 H0 recommendation said the tightened kernel-of-truth should read: 'Combining g† dimensionally with a density and an acceleration to back-solve a third density is dimensionally consistent' — language that exactly mirrors the dome's actual formula rho_A = g0 × rho_bar / g† (which uses three inputs: g0, rho_bar, g†). The decider's self-applied patch instead substituted: 'combining it dimensionally with c to extract a density is dimensionally self-consistent' (sections.json:part1.html ~idx 35093). Two problems: (a) MISREPRESENTATION — the dome's formula at model.html ~line 629 (verified live by c1 2026-06-13) does NOT use c; it uses g0 and rho_bar. A knowledgeable defender will say 'you don't understand our published formula — we never combined g† with c.' (b) DIMENSIONAL ANALYSIS FAILS AT THE DOME'S OWN NUMBER — the natural a0^2/(G·c^2) combination of g† with c via Milgrom-style cosmology gives 2.4e-27 kg/m^3 (cosmic critical-density scale; own arithmetic this review: 1.2e-10^2 / (6.674e-11 × 9e16) ~= 2.4e-27), which is 44 orders of magnitude SMALLER than the dome's 3.4e17. So even granting 'g†-and-c is dimensionally consistent for a density,' the resulting density would be cosmic-mean-density-scale, not neutron-star-scale. The patch closes the surface form of the c1 H0 problem (the over-gracious 'kind of move a working theorist would make' framing is gone) but reintroduces a different over-concession — one that misrepresents the dome's actual derivation pathway and concedes a dimensional argument that, if taken seriously, would yield a density 44 orders of magnitude off from the dome's published value.
holes_found.recommendation: Replace the phrase 'combining it dimensionally with c to extract a density is dimensionally self-consistent' (~idx 35093) with the c1 recommendation's literal language: 'combining g† dimensionally with another density and an acceleration scale to back-solve a third density is dimensionally consistent.' This (a) matches the dome's actual rho_A = g0 × rho_bar / g† formula structure (three inputs, not g†-and-c), (b) avoids the dimensional-analysis-by-44-orders-of-magnitude trap, (c) preserves the c1's intent of conceding the dimensional move while pinning the error upstream on lack of theoretical motivation. Decider can patch as a narrow string replacement.

holes_found.description: MINOR REDUNDANCY in the patched kernel-of-truth paragraph. The patched text says 'MOND treats g† as a transition scale for galactic dynamics; there is no MOND-theoretical — or any-theoretical — justification for interpreting it as a medium density.' Then immediately follows: 'The McGaugh relation describes gravitational accelerations in low-acceleration regimes of galactic dynamics — it is not a constraint on a medium that human beings walk through.' Both clauses make essentially the same point (galactic-dynamics scope of g†, not a medium-density constraint). The first half supplies the MOND-specific reason; the second half restates the scope point in different words. Reads as belt-and-braces but lay readers may parse it as repetitive. Not a hole in the argument — a polish opportunity.
holes_found.recommendation: Optional: collapse the two clauses to one, e.g. 'MOND treats g† as a transition scale for galactic dynamics — it constrains low-acceleration galactic motion, not a medium that human beings walk through. Importing the value without auditing what it means for ordinary motion is the error.' Decider's call; the current text is clear enough.

holes_found.description: H4 LEFT INTACT AS WONTFIX (ISS-2758 noted as 'optional quantitative enhancement, wontfix; the qualitative point stands and quantifying this would require a citation'). The patched text still reads 'vaporizes it instantly' (sections.json:part1.html ~idx 36000). This was the c1's optional rhetorical sharpening. Per c1: actual power deposition at v=10 m/s, A=100 m^2 through 3.4e17 kg/m^3 is ~1.7e22 W (own arithmetic), i.e. ~1/22,000th of solar luminosity into one airframe per second — vastly exceeds 'vaporization'. The decision to wontfix is defensible (the qualitative point lands; quantifying needs a citation; lay-reader register favors the current phrasing). Flagging only for the record — not a hole in c2.
holes_found.recommendation: No action. If the operator later wants maximum impact, the c1 H4 recommendation ('dumps roughly 10^22 W into the airframe per square meter of frontal area — comparable to stellar-interior energy densities') is on the shelf. For now, leave alone.

stronger_arguments.description: AUDIT-THE-DERIVATION (carried forward from c1 stronger_arguments). Dome publishes rho_A = g0 × rho_bar / g† at model.html ~line 629 but never defines rho_bar. Back-solving for rho_bar that yields 3.4e17 at g0=9.81 and g†=1.2e-10 gives rho_bar ~= 4.16e6 kg/m^3 — denser than Earth's core (1.3e4), thinner than white-dwarf interior (~1e9), and matching no standard cosmological or galactic mean density (cosmic mean ~9.5e-27). This is a separate kill from medium-incoherence: the published number is the output of an unauditable derivation whose middle term has no defined physical meaning. Could be added as a one-paragraph footnote. Not necessary for the current argument but available as escalation, and if Hole 0 (mistranscription) gets patched, the audit-the-derivation point becomes natural follow-on text.

kernel_of_truth.description: The patched §1.5 subsection makes the right structural choice: engage the actual published number (3.4e17 kg/m^3 from model.html, verified by c1 at sections.json:part1.html idx 33823 forward), credit the McGaugh radial acceleration relation as a genuine empirical regularity (sections.json:part1.html ~idx 34915 cites g† ~= 1.2e-10 m/s^2 SPARC, verified by c1), then show that even with full credit to the empirical input, the dome's derived value is incompatible with motion through the medium. The dimensional-incompatibility argument lands — a 14-order-of-magnitude-denser-than-water medium genuinely cannot be the same thing that walks through humans, pushes aircraft, and bends light. The c1 framing — 'engage the actual claim, then show that even granting the dimensional move, the resulting number is incompatible with ordinary motion' — is preserved structurally by the patched text and remains correct.
kernel_of_truth.why_it_doesnt_save_claim: Crediting the empirical SPARC input does not validate the dome's specific 3.4e17 kg/m^3 number. The kill turns on a separate observation: any medium at that density that is ALSO asserted to (a) push aircraft as a slipstream (sections.json:part1.html earlier §1.5 'Job 2' framing, anchored at the JFK-LHR-asymmetry argument), and (b) metric-warp ground distance (Sydney-Perth 'Job 3' framing same subsection) must mechanically interact with ordinary matter — and the dome publishes the density without ever computing what that interaction would do. The c1 cross-reference to §1.7 (Gravity Paradox, verified at sections.json:part1.html idx 64171) documents the parallel gap for gravity. The kernel-of-truth saves the dome from a strawman charge; it does not save 3.4e17 kg/m^3 from a Sydney-Perth airframe (own arithmetic c1: 1.7e22 W power deposition at v=10 m/s, A=100 m^2; this c2 confirms a0^2/(G·c^2) ~= 2.4e-27 kg/m^3, the dimensionally-natural g†-and-c density, is 44 orders of magnitude smaller than the dome's published value — which is the H0c2 finding above).

deeper_analysis: The c1 review identified one moderate hole (H0 kernel-of-truth over-generosity) and three minor holes (H1 saturation arithmetic, H2 'factor of unity' phrasing, H3 'same gap' vs 'same shape of gap'). The decider self-applied all four (H4 was noted-but-wontfixed per ISS-2758). This c2 confirms that H1, H2, H3 landed verbatim against the c1 recommendations and close their respective complaints fully. H0 is the interesting case: the patch closed the c1's specific surface complaint (the 'kind of move a working theorist would make' over-grace is gone) but the decider's wording substitution — 'with c' instead of the c1 recommendation's 'with a density and an acceleration' — introduces a new technical imprecision. The dome's actual formula at model.html ~line 629 is rho_A = g0 × rho_bar / g† (three inputs: g0, rho_bar, g†; verified by c1 2026-06-13). 'Combining g† with c' is not what the dome does. And the dimensional Milgrom-style combination a0^2/(G·c^2) gives 2.4e-27 kg/m^3 (cosmic-density scale; verified by own arithmetic this review: 1.44e-20 / (6.67e-11 × 9e16) = 2.4e-27) — 44 orders of magnitude away from the dome's 3.4e17. So the patched concession 'dimensionally self-consistent with c' is doubly weak: it concedes a derivation pathway the dome doesn't use, and that pathway wouldn't even yield the dome's published value. A knowledgeable defender could pull the thread: 'you don't understand our published formula' is a usable deflection. The fix is small — drop 'with c' for the c1's literal recommendation language. This is a calibration finding for the decider: when c1 recommendations include load-bearing technical phrasing (which c1 H0's recommendation deliberately did, mirroring the dome's three-input formula), self-applied patches should track the recommendation verbatim, not paraphrase. The broader argument (medium-incompatible-with-motion, neutron-star-density-as-walking-medium, parallel gap to §1.7 gravity-paradox) stands and continues to be one of the cleanest single-paragraph kills in the review. No verdict change. Recommend minor_edit to close H0c2.
